bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Adverse climatic conditions affecting cane availability — The potential development of El Nino conditions may bring below-normal rainfall, affecting sugarcane availability, crop yields and sugar recovery, with a direct impact on crushing operations and overall production. Because cane is sourced entirely from the local command area around Lakhimpur Kheri, the Division has no alternative supply pool. Mitigation rests on the Cane Excellence Programme - varietal replacement, scientific agronomic practices and mechanisation.
- Low cane yield and declining sugar recovery — Sub-optimal cane productivity is a key operational risk with knock-on implications for sugar recovery and for ethanol and power output, since all three products draw on the same cane throughput. Sugar recovery already moderated to 10.26% in FY26 from 10.61%, in line with regional trends. Addressed through demonstration plots, soil health management, precision nutrient application and farmer training.
- Regulatory intervention in sugar and ethanol pricing and offtake — The sugar industry operates within a dynamic regulatory environment where government policy sets cane pricing, ethanol procurement terms and sugar sales quotas. Sugar sales fell 5.4% year-on-year purely on a lower government-released quota, exports were moved from Restricted to Prohibited until 30 September 2026, and FRP and State Advised Price were both raised for the 2025-26 season, compressing the spread between an administered input cost and a quota-constrained output. The Company diversifies its ethanol feedstock mix and optimises production planning to retain flexibility.
- Commodity and inventory price volatility in sugar and ethanol — Key commodities remain exposed to price volatility. Ethanol prices are largely regulated, so the Company cannot price its way out of an input-cost rise, while sugar prices are shaped by government policy, cane pricing and market dynamics. The Company monitors market trends and aligns its sales strategy to manage pricing risk.
- Real estate demand volatility and interest rate sensitivity — Real estate demand is sensitive to inflation, interest rates, employment, consumer sentiment, taxation and property prices, while raw material price movements can compress project costs and margins. Separately, interest rate movements affect borrowing costs, property valuations and investment activity across the division. Mitigated through timely execution, experienced contractors, long-standing supplier relationships and local sourcing.
- Interest rate and liquidity exposure on borrowings — Borrowings linked to floating rates are exposed to changes in market interest rates, and maintaining adequate liquidity to meet operational requirements and financial commitments is stated as a key priority. Managed through prudent debt management, hedging where considered necessary, disciplined cash flow planning, working capital monitoring and liquidity buffers. The Company reports no foreign currency borrowings and therefore limited direct FX exposure.
- Climate risk across both operating divisions — Climate-related events present operational challenges group-wide: adverse weather can delay construction schedules and site productivity in real estate, while rainfall variability affects sugarcane availability, yield and quality in the SPE business. Weather-related assessments are integrated into operational planning.
- Cyber security exposure across an increasingly digital operating model — Cyber security is recognised within the enterprise risk assessment, a material concern given the Company's heavy reliance on digital platforms (SAP, SPE BI Cockpit, Saksham, GPS tracking, Power BI dashboards) for cane procurement, plant monitoring and sales. Addressed through regular security assessments, continuous network monitoring, robust backup mechanisms and periodic system upgrades.
- Concentration of core manufacturing in a single site — The entire Sugar, Power & Ethanol Division - the Company's principal operating business - runs from one integrated complex at Gobind Sugar Mills, Aira, in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, with cane drawn wholly from the surrounding command area. This is a structural single-site and single-region concentration, and it compounds the climatic and yield risks the Company discloses separately.

outlook.body: Zuari Industries' principal capacity asset is the fully integrated Sugar, Power & Ethanol complex at Gobind Sugar Mills, Aira, in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, comprising a 10,000 TCD sugar mill, a 500 TPD sugar refinery, a 40 MW cogeneration power plant and a 125 KLPD distillery operating as a unified value chain. The most significant addition during FY26 was the commissioning on 1 January 2026 of a 180 KLPD grain-based ethanol distillery at Lakhimpur through the 50:50 joint venture Zuari Envien Bioenergy Private Limited; built as a Zero Liquid Discharge facility processing maize and broken rice to produce fuel ethanol and DDGS, it commenced commercial production during the year and has since been stabilised, securing non-OMC orders pending the second OMC tender, with the focus now on optimising feedstock sourcing and maximising plant utilisation. Existing plant capacity was pushed to its highest-ever utilisation of 101.7% during FY26 through process optimisation and digital tools rather than new capital assets. Expansion elsewhere in the group is deliberately asset-light: Zuari Infraworld added Development Management mandates with an aggregate Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 5,000 crore covering a commercial office project under construction in Kolkata, a large residential development at launch stage in Hyderabad and further residential and mixed-use projects in design and approval, while entering Bengaluru; its Dubai St. Regis Residences (232 residences across approximately 8.06 lakh sq. ft., a 50:50 joint venture) reached completion and entered handover, and Phase IV of Zuari Garden City, Mysore (156 residential plots on the 73.5-acre township) is fully developed and ready for handover. In real estate the Company has completed a feasibility study for Phase II of the Zuari Rain Forest Project in Goa and is evaluating the strategic options identified, while continuing to pursue value-accretive monetisation of approximately 523 acres owned at Sancoale Village, South Goa. The Company states it is enhancing existing operations while evaluating inorganic opportunities aligned with its long-term objectives. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum for the Company's own capex is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Ethanol demand underpinned by the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme reaching the 20% blending target in ESY 2025-26, five years ahead of the original 2030 timeline, with policy focus now shifting to blends beyond E20 and notification of E22, E25, E27 and E30 fuel standards
- Feedstock diversification across B-heavy and C-heavy molasses, sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, maize, damaged food grains and FCI rice has reduced single-crop dependence and improved year-round ethanol availability and distillery utilisation
- Sugar realisations supported by firm domestic prices and balanced market fundamentals; Company average sugar realisation improved 4.1% year-on-year to Rs 4,053 per quintal
- Sugar volumes constrained by the government-released sales quota - sugar sales fell 5.4% year-on-year despite record crushing
- Sugar recovery moderated to 10.26% from 10.61%, in line with lower recovery trends across the region, partially offsetting higher cane throughput
- Government revised cane pricing for the 2025-26 crushing season - FRP raised by Rs 15 to Rs 355 per quintal and State Advised Price raised by Rs 30 to Rs 400 per quintal for early varieties and Rs 390 for general varieties - which raises input cost
- Sugar exports moved from Restricted to Prohibited until 30 September 2026, confining sales to the domestic market
- Draft Sugarcane (Control) Order, 2026 proposes to recognise ethanol as a core output of sugar mills and introduces an equivalence framework for ethanol in regulatory assessments, retaining the FRP mechanism
- IMD has indicated likely El Nino conditions during the 2026 southwest monsoon, raising the probability of below-normal rainfall and pressure on cane yields and recovery, though irrigation-supported Uttar Pradesh is expected to remain relatively resilient
- Indian real estate demand driven by premium and luxury housing, GCC-led office absorption and infrastructure-led government capex, with residential sales value growth expected to moderate to 4-6% in FY2027
- Improved operating efficiencies, prudent financial management and a lower cost of borrowing cited by management as the drivers of the year's improved profitability
- Ethanol production growth supported by improved distillery utilisation, with operating days rising from 288 in FY25 to 316 in FY26
- Simon India secured new orders worth Rs 100.3 crore during FY26, including a large-capacity phosphoric acid tank project from PPL Mangalore, an Oil & Gas project from HMEL, and a cost estimation assignment for a major DAP/NPK project for CFCL
- Simon India had an order book of Rs 95 crore under execution as stated in the Managing Director's message
- Simon India completed projects worth approximately Rs 50 crore during the year, including the fifth evaporator project and an 8,000-tonne phosphoric acid tank for Paradeep Phosphates
- Zuari Infraworld expanded its Development Management portfolio during the year with mandates carrying an aggregate Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 5,000 crore, spanning a commercial office project under construction in Kolkata, a large residential development in Hyderabad at launch stage, and several residential and mixed-use projects in design and approval stages (sourced from the Corporate Overview section of the capex bundle)
- Zuari Garden City, Mysore Phase IV, comprising 156 residential plots, is fully developed and ready for handover with nearly 80% of inventory already sold
- The St. Regis Residences, Downtown Dubai - 232 ultra-luxury residences across approximately 8.06 lakh sq. ft. - is completely sold out and has entered the handover and possession phase
- Zuari Envien Bioenergy secured orders from non-OMC customers pending the second OMC tender

one_liner.body: Zuari Industries Limited is the apex holding company of the Adventz Group, operating a fully integrated Sugar, Power & Ethanol complex in Uttar Pradesh alongside substantial Goa land holdings and a portfolio of engineering, real estate, consumer and financial-services subsidiaries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The core operating business is the Sugar, Power & Ethanol (SPE) Division at Gobind Sugar Mills, Aira, in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, where sugar manufacturing, cogeneration, ethanol production and sugar refining run as a single integrated value chain, with cane sourced entirely from the local command area. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ethanol demand underpinned by the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme reaching the 20% blending target in ESY 2025-26, five years ahead of the original 2030 timeline, with policy focus now shifting to blends beyond E20 and notification of E22, E25, E27 and E30 fuel standards
- Feedstock diversification across B-heavy and C-heavy molasses, sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, maize, damaged food grains and FCI rice has reduced single-crop dependence and improved year-round ethanol availability and distillery utilisation
- Sugar realisations supported by firm domestic prices and balanced market fundamentals; Company average sugar realisation improved 4.1% year-on-year to Rs 4,053 per quintal
- Sugar volumes constrained by the government-released sales quota - sugar sales fell 5.4% year-on-year despite record crushing
- Sugar recovery moderated to 10.26% from 10.61%, in line with lower recovery trends across the region, partially offsetting higher cane throughput
- Government revised cane pricing for the 2025-26 crushing season - FRP raised by Rs 15 to Rs 355 per quintal and State Advised Price raised by Rs 30 to Rs 400 per quintal for early varieties and Rs 390 for general varieties - which raises input cost
- Sugar exports moved from Restricted to Prohibited until 30 September 2026, confining sales to the domestic market
- Draft Sugarcane (Control) Order, 2026 proposes to recognise ethanol as a core output of sugar mills and introduces an equivalence framework for ethanol in regulatory assessments, retaining the FRP mechanism
- IMD has indicated likely El Nino conditions during the 2026 southwest monsoon, raising the probability of below-normal rainfall and pressure on cane yields and recovery, though irrigation-supported Uttar Pradesh is expected to remain relatively resilient
- Indian real estate demand driven by premium and luxury housing, GCC-led office absorption and infrastructure-led government capex, with residential sales value growth expected to moderate to 4-6% in FY2027
- Improved operating efficiencies, prudent financial management and a lower cost of borrowing cited by management as the drivers of the year's improved profitability
- Ethanol production growth supported by improved distillery utilisation, with operating days rising from 288 in FY25 to 316 in FY26
- Simon India secured new orders worth Rs 100.3 crore during FY26, including a large-capacity phosphoric acid tank project from PPL Mangalore, an Oil & Gas project from HMEL, and a cost estimation assignment for a major DAP/NPK project for CFCL
- Simon India had an order book of Rs 95 crore under execution as stated in the Managing Director's message
- Simon India completed projects worth approximately Rs 50 crore during the year, including the fifth evaporator project and an 8,000-tonne phosphoric acid tank for Paradeep Phosphates
- Zuari Infraworld expanded its Development Management portfolio during the year with mandates carrying an aggregate Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 5,000 crore, spanning a commercial office project under construction in Kolkata, a large residential development in Hyderabad at launch stage, and several residential and mixed-use projects in design and approval stages (sourced from the Corporate Overview section of the capex bundle)
- Zuari Garden City, Mysore Phase IV, comprising 156 residential plots, is fully developed and ready for handover with nearly 80% of inventory already sold
- The St. Regis Residences, Downtown Dubai - 232 ultra-luxury residences across approximately 8.06 lakh sq. ft. - is completely sold out and has entered the handover and possession phase
- Zuari Envien Bioenergy secured orders from non-OMC customers pending the second OMC tender

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Zuari Industries' principal capacity asset is the fully integrated Sugar, Power & Ethanol complex at Gobind Sugar Mills, Aira, in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, comprising a 10,000 TCD sugar mill, a 500 TPD sugar refinery, a 40 MW cogeneration power plant and a 125 KLPD distillery operating as a unified value chain. The most significant addition during FY26 was the commissioning on 1 January 2026 of a 180 KLPD grain-based ethanol distillery at Lakhimpur through the 50:50 joint venture Zuari Envien Bioenergy Private Limited; built as a Zero Liquid Discharge facility processing maize and broken rice to produce fuel ethanol and DDGS, it commenced commercial production during the year and has since been stabilised, securing non-OMC orders pending the second OMC tender, with the focus now on optimising feedstock sourcing and maximising plant utilisation. Existing plant capacity was pushed to its highest-ever utilisation of 101.7% during FY26 through process optimisation and digital tools rather than new capital assets. Expansion elsewhere in the group is deliberately asset-light: Zuari Infraworld added Development Management mandates with an aggregate Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 5,000 crore covering a commercial office project under construction in Kolkata, a large residential development at launch stage in Hyderabad and further residential and mixed-use projects in design and approval, while entering Bengaluru; its Dubai St. Regis Residences (232 residences across approximately 8.06 lakh sq. ft., a 50:50 joint venture) reached completion and entered handover, and Phase IV of Zuari Garden City, Mysore (156 residential plots on the 73.5-acre township) is fully developed and ready for handover. In real estate the Company has completed a feasibility study for Phase II of the Zuari Rain Forest Project in Goa and is evaluating the strategic options identified, while continuing to pursue value-accretive monetisation of approximately 523 acres owned at Sancoale Village, South Goa. The Company states it is enhancing existing operations while evaluating inorganic opportunities aligned with its long-term objectives. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum for the Company's own capex is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.
